overview: Microscopy is the field concerned with Seeing the small: light, electron, and probe microscopes revealing worlds beyond the naked eye. Deconvolution belongs to its essential core. Concretely: Magnification vs resolution — empty magnification enlarges blur; only resolution reveals detail. And Confocal microscopy — laser scanning with pinholes rejecting out-of-focus blur for 3D images. Mastering this entry means being able to explain the topic in plain sentences, recognize it in real cases, and apply it alongside the neighboring ideas of the Advanced tier.
core_concepts: Magnification vs resolution: empty magnification enlarges blur; only resolution reveals detail.
Confocal microscopy: laser scanning with pinholes rejecting out-of-focus blur for 3D images.
key_laws: Nyquist sampling: pixels smaller than half the resolution to preserve detail.
Abbe diffraction limit: resolution about wavelength over twice the numerical aperture.
vocabulary: Super-resolution: techniques beating the diffraction limit with clever fluorophore control.
Working distance: the gap between lens and sample, traded against resolution.
methods: Deconvolution: computational reassignment of blurred light to its source.
